summary: Mud Lake Lookout in the Bob Marshall Wilderness: a 1932 L-4 cab, abandoned in 1972, restored by volunteers by 2020 and assessed again in 2025.

access.note: Abandoned in 1972; no rental or public visiting program found. Reached on foot through the Bob Marshall Wilderness.

visit.trail_note: About 2.5 miles one way on foot, with blowdown and a ford to cross (2025 crew report).

events.note: Gable-roofed L-4 cab built; the register says it keeps the original gabled roof.
firelookout.com lists known lookout personnel for 1957.
A forest fire threatened the lookout. The register does not say it burned.
Volunteer restoration completed in August, per the 2020 year-end report.
Registered as NHLR US 1496 (MT 74) on January 9, 2021.
Crew assessment; the lookout is listed under assessments in the chapter's 2025 report.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources give 1921 and 1932. The site was established with a camp in 1921, and the gable-roofed L-4 cab that stands was built in 1932. Both are recorded.
NHLR gives 6,335 ft (1,931 m) and firelookout.com gives 6361 ft. The brief's 1930.9 m matches the NHLR figure, which the record keeps.

sources.title: Northwest Montana Lookout Association year-end report 2020

notes_for_editor: The brief's 1932 build and 1972 abandonment hold. The 1921 camp date reconciles the build-year conflict in the brief. The brief's kind ground is not supported by any page read, so it was not recorded. Current condition after the 2025 assessment is not confirmed: only the report excerpt was read. The 2000 fire is recorded as a threat only; no source says it burned. Four page reads and one WebSearch used.
